documents.title: Diagnosing application database connection-pool exhaustion
documents.body: Symptoms: requests time out waiting for a database connection while direct database network health checks succeed. Check active, idle, and maximum pool counts; inspect connection acquisition wait duration; compare application concurrency with configured pool limits. If all connections are active, inspect long-running transactions and leaked sessions before increasing the pool. Confirm database-side connection limits before any sizing change. Recommended response: identify the consuming request path, close leaked transactions, and adjust pool/concurrency together within the database connection budget. Verify acquisition waits and error rate return to baseline.

documents.title: Worker startup failure after a release
documents.body: Symptoms: a worker starts after deployment and exits before subscribing to its queue. Read startup and configuration-loader logs in timestamp order. A missing required configuration value is a likely cause when initialization aborts before queue subscription. Compare the current release's declared configuration requirements with the deployment environment. Do not expose secret values in logs or reports; check presence and versioned configuration names only. Roll back or restore the missing setting through the approved configuration process, then verify worker readiness and queue subscription.

documents.title: Responding to application-node disk pressure
documents.body: Symptoms: filesystem utilization approaches capacity and writes fail with no space left on device. Confirm which mount is full and correlate usage growth with log, cache, or data directories. Preserve evidence before removing files. Apply retention or rotation through the normal process and verify that application data is intact. Do not delete active data files. Recheck filesystem headroom and write health after remediation.

documents.title: Investigating service dependency timeouts
documents.body: Symptoms: local service readiness passes but requests to one dependency time out and a circuit breaker opens. Compare dependency latency, timeout threshold, retry count, and failure timestamps. Check dependency health before changing client behavior. Avoid multiplying load through aggressive retries. A sustained dependency outage may require dependency-owner action; local timeout tuning is not a substitute for restoring dependency health. Confirm recovery using successful dependency calls and a closed circuit breaker.

documents.title: TLS certificate expiry at a public listener
documents.body: Symptoms: clients fail the TLS handshake while the listener process remains healthy. Check certificate subject, expiry timestamp, and the certificate currently presented by the affected listener. Renew through the normal certificate authority and deployment procedure; never place private key material in incident logs. Verify the chain and expiry from the listener after reload, then confirm a representative handshake succeeds.

documents.title: Queue backlog with a stale consumer
documents.body: Symptoms: broker connection is established, queue depth grows, and acknowledgements stop. Inspect consumer-loop health, acknowledgement timestamps, worker resource usage, and recent deploys. Separate a broker outage from a stalled consumer by checking connectivity and delivery/acknowledgement progress. Restore the consumer safely and monitor queue age and depth until they decline.

documents.title: Schema compatibility during a staged rollout
documents.body: Symptoms: errors appear on only some replicas during a staged rollout and identify different schema or mapping versions. Compare replica release versions, migration state, and expected schema compatibility. Pause rollout progression while confirming backward compatibility. Roll back or complete a compatible migration using the normal release procedure, then verify all replicas serve the same supported schema.

documents.title: Handling isolated latency samples without a clear cause
documents.body: A single slow request without correlated resource, dependency, or error evidence is not enough to identify a root cause. Compare a larger time window, request percentiles, affected routes, and neighboring service telemetry. Report uncertainty and gather more observations when evidence remains sparse. Do not recommend a state change based on an isolated latency sample.
